story.title: Aruṇa and Bhrāmarī
story.scope: Devī Bhāgavata10.13.33–127; opening six-Manu account excluded from this bounded arc
story.completeness_basis: Bounded narrative chronology checked against whole cited English body; no exhaustive Sanskrit atomic completeness or other recension equivalence claimed.
story.editorial_notes: Translation narrator statements and attributed dialogue distinguished. No remembered details added; unknown spouse/mother/guru fields remain unstated.

events.details: Aruṇa lives in a nether Daitya city, then undertakes Brahmā worship beside Ganges in Himalaya. Four successive10,000year stages use dry leaves, water drops, air and finally no food; he repeats Gāyatrī continuously. His ascetic heat threatens worlds; gods petition Brahmā. Brahmā appears with Gāyatrī and four Vedas.

Aruṇa first requests immortality. Brahmā refuses an impossible boon and says Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva too are mortal. Aruṇa revises the request to the specified war/weapon/sex/limb-category death exclusions and strength to conquer gods. Brahmā assents.
events.outcome: A qualified boon, not universal immortality, is granted.

events.details: Aruṇa gathers nether Daityas, sends a messenger to Indra and conquers heaven, taking forms/offices of sun, moon, Yama, Agni and others through ascetic power. Gods seek counsel with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva at Kailāsa.

A heavenly voice directs worship of the world Queen and identifies cessation of Gāyatrī repetition as the condition making Aruṇa killable. Indra sends Bṛhaspati; gods perform Devī sacrifice and Māyā-bīja worship. Bṛhaspati approaches as a muni and argues that sharing the gods’ Goddess worship undermines Aruṇa’s hostility. Aruṇa abandons Gāyatrī through pride and loses strength; Bṛhaspati reports success.
events.outcome: Gods continue worship; a long interval of unspecified duration follows.

events.details: After continued worship Bhrāmarī appears with diverse garments and ornaments, bees in her fists and garland, and boon/fearlessness gestures. Bee sound is associated with Hrīm. Gods offer an extended hymn, then describe Aruṇa’s boon and injuries. Hymnic names are attributed praise, not separate narrated births.

Bhrāmarī releases bees/hornets from every side. Their multitude covers the world and attacks the Daityas’ chests. The text denies the foes time or capacity to fight, wield weapons or speak; principal Daityas perish immediately. Bees return to the Goddess; gods rejoice with praise, music and dance.
events.outcome: Aruṇa’s forces perish; no negotiated surrender.

events.details: The Goddess grants separate boons to the gods, whose individual contents are not specified here, and grants their express request for unshakeable devotion. She disappears; Nārāyaṇa concludes with liberation promised for hearing the account.
